title: Ensuring Concrete Improvements to Vehicular Safety Practices following January 2026's Voluntary Safety Time-out
what_it_is: Ensuring Concrete Improvements to Vehicular Safety Practices following January 2026's Voluntary Safety Time-out

sections.label: Voluntary Safety Time-out vehicular safety
sections.summary: MOM called a voluntary Safety Time-out from 13 to 27 January 2026 on vehicular safety after four December vehicle-related workplace fatalities, with no inspections or enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) had called for a voluntary Safety Time-out from 13 to 27 January 2026, focusing on vehicular safety because of four vehicle-related workplace fatalities in December.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The objective of the Safety Time-out was to remind companies to take time off from their regular work routine to review and ensure that appropriate safety measures and procedures were in place, and for workers to refresh their knowledge of these procedures and to stay vigilant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In line with the voluntary nature of the Safety Time-out, there were no inspections nor enforcement actions.

sections.label: January inspections and enforcement actions
sections.summary: Around 500 inspections were conducted in January, with three stop-work orders and five fines issued for vehicle-related breaches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Around 500 inspections have been conducted in January.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Three stop-work orders and five fines were issued to companies and individuals for vehicle-related breaches.

sections.label: Productivity Solutions Grant vehicle safety
sections.summary: The Productivity Solutions Grant defrays 50% of funding up to $30,000; about 1,000 companies adopted vehicle safety technologies, with about $12.5 million dispensed as at July 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: On the question that the Member had on grants, I want to just highlight that we have the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) that small and medium enterprises can tap upon, where 50% of funding can be defrayed, for up to a cap of $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: And as at July 2025, about 1,000 companies have adopted vehicle safety technologies via the PSG, and a total of about $12.5 million has been dispensed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash
sentences.text: As to whether or not for it to be mandated, I think we take a holistic and calibrated approach to all the solutions as well as the situation that we have.
